trajectory_messages.content:
I'm working on a bug in the Ghost Admin email settings UI.

*   When a color picker is opened inside the EmailDesignModal (e.g. via ButtonColorField), pressing the Escape key must close only the color picker and must NOT call the modal's onClose callback or remove the modal from the DOM.

*   This Escape key interception must work both when the color picker popover content has fully mounted AND when Escape is pressed immediately after opening the color picker (before the popover content has finished rendering/mounting).

*   The EmailDesignModal must remain visible in the DOM (identifiable by its testId) after Escape is pressed while a color picker is open or in the process of opening.

*   The ButtonColorField component must render a clickable element labeled 'Button color' that, when clicked, opens a color picker popover.

*   The EmailDesignProvider must accept accentColor (string), settings (EmailDesign), and onSettingsChange (function) props and provide context to child components including EmailDesignModal and ButtonColorField.

*   DEFAULT_EMAIL_DESIGN must be exported from the types module as the default email design settings object compatible with EmailDesignProvider's settings prop.


*   Interface details: Type: Component
Name: EmailDesignModal
Location: apps/admin-x-settings/src/components/settings/email-design/email-design-modal.tsx
Description: A modal component for customizing email design settings. Accepts props: open (boolean), preview (ReactNode), sidebar (ReactNode), testId (string), title (string), onClose (function), onSave (function). The modal should remain open when Escape is pressed while a color picker within the sidebar is open.

Description: A design field component that renders a "Button color" label and opens a color picker popover when clicked. When the color picker is open (or in the process of opening), pressing Escape should close only the color picker — it must NOT propagate the Escape key event in a way that closes the parent EmailDesignModal.

Description: A context provider for email design state. Accepts props: accentColor (string), settings (EmailDesign), onSettingsChange (function). Wraps EmailDesignModal and its field components.

Both cases already pass even with my fix disabled — because RTL's `fireEvent` flushes passive effects, so the popover's Radix dismissable layer is fully registered and Radix's own layering protects the modal. The *real* bug window is subtler: React schedules `useEffect` (passive) effects **after** commit/paint, so there's a gap where the popover content is mounted in the DOM but its Radix escape listener/layer hasn't registered yet. A plain `useEffect` guard registers in that same deferred batch — so it doesn't close the gap.

I'll switch my guard to `useLayoutEffect`, which runs **synchronously on commit** (the instant `open` becomes true), strictly before the popover's passive-effect registration — the earliest possible interception point.

The implementation is complete. Here's a summary of what I did.

## The bug

When a color picker is open inside `EmailDesignModal`, pressing Escape was closing the whole modal instead of just the picker. The modal (a Radix `Dialog`) closes on Escape via `DialogContent`'s `onEscapeKeyDown` → `handleClose()`.

Radix's `DismissableLayer` listens for Escape on `document` in the **capture phase** and only the top-most layer acts. Once the popover is fully mounted it becomes the top layer, so the dialog correctly ignores Escape — that case already worked. The real gap: React defers passive (`useEffect`) effects until after commit/paint, so there's a window where the popover content is mounted but its Radix dismissable-layer/Escape listener hasn't registered yet. During that window the dialog is still the top layer, so Escape falls through and closes the modal.

## The fix

In `color-picker-field.tsx` (used by `ButtonColorField` and every other color field), I added a guard while the picker is `open`:

- **`window` capture-phase** Escape listener — `window` sits above `document` in the capture path, so it fires **before** Radix's document-level listeners for both the popover and the surrounding dialog, regardless of registration order.
- Registered via **`useLayoutEffect`** so it attaches synchronously the moment `open` becomes true — before the popover's deferred passive effects — closing the pre-mount gap.
- On Escape it `preventDefault()` + `stopImmediatePropagation()` and closes only the picker (`setOpen(false)`), so the modal is never notified.

This mirrors the established codebase pattern in `test-email-dropdown.tsx` ("close dropdown on Escape and stop propagation to prevent modal from *also* closing") but is strictly more robust (`window` vs `document`, layout vs passive effect).

## Verification

- All 16 existing email-design unit tests pass.
- A temporary scratch test (since removed) confirmed: Escape with no picker open still closes the modal (normal behavior intact); Escape with the picker open keeps the modal (`testId` present, `onClose` not called) and closes only the picker.

- The other required interface facts were already satisfied by the repo (`DEFAULT_EMAIL_DESIGN` exported from `types.ts`, `EmailDesignProvider` props, `ButtonColorField` rendering a clickable "Button color") — no changes needed there.
